components.gap: Every element of the success condition is present for the weights, heterogeneity and interval procedures, but two owed derivation steps are not written, so for two selected procedures the claim that the stated dependence/common-effect assumption yields the stated conclusion is asserted rather than derived. (1) thm:p15-synthesis-linear (body lines 143-146) asserts that a_*^T Y +/- z sqrt(V_*) is an exact 1-alpha interval when Y is 'multivariate normal' with known general covariance; 'multivariate normal' is defined nowhere on the handbook route, and annex lines 52-55 prove normality of the weighted combination only for independent estimates (via thm:p15-normal-sums) and dispose of the dependent case with 'the covariance representation gives the general case' (a sketch), so the exact uncertainty of the dependent-estimate GLS procedure is not derived. (2) thm:p15-synthesis-table-delta (body lines 274-275) asserts consistency of the Mantel-Haenszel risk-ratio estimate under a common risk ratio; annex lines 149-150 discharge it 'by the same argument' without writing the risk-ratio limiting sums or the summand-ratio step (a 'similarly' step). The OR case, delta variance, Peto, DL, Q-profile, REML, I^2, fixed-shape HKSJ, known-tau prediction and Bayesian derivations are written.

Interpretation not counted against C02 and left for the owner's decision: 'selected weighted-estimate procedures' was read as the procedures the treatment selects (extent: 'formula/method dependencies actually used'). Under a reading that owes every weighted-estimate procedure of secs. 10.1-10.14, further underived items would be: MH risk difference (source sec. 10.4; supplement p. 5), the supplement's MH log-OR/log-RR standard-error formulas (pp. 4-5; replaced by the handbook's own large-arm delta variance, body 295-298), meta-regression (source sec. 10.11.4; body 576-578, cautions only), and the O-E/V time-to-event method (source sec. 10.9; body 207-210, mentioned only).

Peto approximate SE (sum V_i)^(-1/2) is used without derivation; annex lines 127-128 state only that an approximately quadratic log likelihood 'motivates' it. Declared approximation, not a claimed result.

Unsupported asides inside definitions: 'With another heterogeneity estimator, such as REML, they need not be identical' (447) has no instance; 'HKSJ can be narrower than Wald when q_H is small' (476-477) has no instance, though it follows directly from the displayed formulas.
